Prevention: Harrow the field to expose larvae to sunlight to kill them.
Incorporate all crop residues from the previous season into the soil (ploughing).
Establish maize trap barriers around eggplant plots 15 days before transplanting.
Conserve natural enemies by avoiding broad-spectrum insecticides and providing suitable habitat.
Raise seedlings far away from sources of infestation (old eggplant fields, eggplant stubble).
Grow seedlings under nylon netting to prevent moths from laying eggs on the plants.
Intercrop with coriander or fennel to reduce pest infestation.
Monitoring: Start monitoring for borers at the early vegetative stage.
Use pheromone traps to monitor adult moths.
Look for drooping tender shoots and wilting.
Observe crops for small exit holes below the calyx of fruits and the presence of larvae inside damaged fruit and shoots.
At crop fruiting stage, look for holes filled with insect excretions.
Look for reddish-translucent larvae or adult moths with white wings and characteristic brown 'heart' patterns.
Follow control actions if 2% of plants or a minimum of 1% of fruit show symptoms.
Direct Control: Practice good farm sanitation, i.e. remove and destroy infested plant materials.
Spray neem oil products (For 1% azadirachtin ~30ml/15L; 0.3% azad. ~75ml/15L).
Contact and ingestion of systemic insecticide.
Restrictions: Rotate chemical use (change chemical regularly) to avoid the build-up of resistance.
Toxic to bees and other non-target arthropods.
Toxic to aquatic organisms, do not use near waterways.
